What comes up in Leppington

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Site cut and levelling on a new estate block

Bringing a greenfield lot to the platform level the civil design calls for.

How it is handled
Topsoil stripped and stockpiled, the cut taken to design level, then fill placed and compacted in layers where the level has to be built up.
What does it
Large excavator, truck and dogs for volume, a roller for compaction.

Clearing an old rural holding

Sheds, fencing, concrete and sometimes a house, on land that is about to be subdivided.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials assessed and removed first, then the structures off and the block left clear for the civil works.
What does it
Midi to large excavator with a grapple, tippers or a truck and dog depending on the volume.

Sheds, garages, pools and outbuildings

Partial demolition, and frequently several structures in one scope with a different waste stream against each.

How it is handled
Taken down separately so the streams stay apart. A pool shell is broken out and removed, then the void is backfilled with suitable material and compacted in layers.
What does it
Mini or midi excavator, a hammer for the pool shell, and tippers rather than a truck and dog on the smaller volumes.

Leppington

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Greenfield growth land There was little standing here to begin with, so the work is site cut, levelling and fill far more often than demolition.
  • Old rural holdings being released Which still carry sheds, fencing, concrete and the occasional house.
  • Earthworks ahead of construction Cut and fill balanced across the site where the design allows it, with imported material placed and compacted in layers.
  • Reactive clay soils Which matter to footing design and to how spoil behaves after rain.

Leppington sites are generally open with room for large plant and good truck access, so the constraint is the programme rather than the block. Where fill is coming in as well as spoil going out, the same truck movement does two jobs and that is worth planning rather than discovering.

Leppington questions

What people ask before we start

Do you do bulk earthworks as well as demolition?
Yes. Bulk excavation, site cut and levelling, and fill supply and placement are all part of the work, and in the growth areas they are most of it.
Can you supply the fill as well as take the spoil?
Yes. Clean fill, virgin excavated natural material and road base are supplied, placed and compacted in layers rather than tipped and spread.
Can you bring fill in as well as take spoil out?
Yes, and where both are needed the same truck movement does two jobs. Clean fill, virgin excavated natural material and road base are supplied and placed, compacted in layers rather than tipped and spread.
How many contractors am I dealing with if there is asbestos on site?
One. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, licensed asbestos removalists carry out the removal, and an independent licensed assessor does the air monitoring and clearance. Sequencing the three of them is our job, not yours.
